_about: Endless mode: one continuous match with no wave cap. Each wave is generated by spending an escalating threat
budget along a composition shape that drifts as the run goes on. A run is fully determined by (seed, tuning).
See ENDLESS_MODE.md for the design and the tuning protocol.
_threat_costs_are_a_measurement: threat_costs are the `threat` column of `scons balance` -- cost per kill against a fixed six-breacher
reference, normalised to grime -- not preferences. They go stale exactly the way the tables in
DIVERSITY_AND_BALANCE.md do: when a unit stat changes, re-run `scons balance` and refresh them here, then
re-run `scons endless` to re-check run length, the not-solved gate and the economy trend.
_level_is_synthesised: Endless is fought on level_05's ground, so the reuse is a narrative fact rather than a shortcut. It authors
no waves at all: the generator supplies every one of them, and an empty wave list is also what makes the HUD
read the wave count as unbounded rather than as a denominator.
_weights_are_bodies_not_budget: A keyframe is a ratio of *units*: {grime: 6, hound: 2} puts six grime and two hounds on the belt. The
generator rescales it by threat_costs before spending the wave budget along it. Authoring it the other way
-- as a share of the budget -- reads the same and behaves nothing like it: grime is the cheapest hostile by
a factor of five, so an even *spend* split is a roster that is almost entirely grime.
_drift_is_the_reason_the_mode_exists: Shape drift is the first content in the game that changes what the player is facing *within* one match. A
campaign level lets the player pick a composition at the start and never revisit the decision; endless makes
the decision recur. The ship gate is that no single friendly mix survives to the target wave across all
seeds -- if one does, these keyframes are wrong and no amount of ramp tuning will fix it.
_set_pieces_break_the_treadmill: Drift alone still reads as monotone, so a degenerate shape lands at intervals. A set piece is the same
generator called with one weight, which is why it costs no new code and no new content. The first match wins,
so a wave that is both a hound wave and a jackal wave is a hound wave.
